config_dir.strict_note: if the variable is set the directory must already exist, or Codex errors out

*.note: same path on darwin, linux and win32; no XDG, no %APPDATA%. Only when Codex is in its default 'file' mode; see 'requires'.

requires.note: 'keyring' keeps the login in the OS keyring (an encrypted file plus a keyring passphrase on Windows) and never reads auth.json; 'auto' prefers the keyring and deletes auth.json after a successful save; 'ephemeral' keeps it in memory. Requirements outrank the user's config, which outranks the system's. Not visible from here: macOS managed preferences, an enterprise cloud bundle, a --profile file, a project's .codex/config.toml and -c on the command line.

liveness.renewed_by_use_note: the date is the access token's expiry, which Codex replaces when it refreshes, so an account in use moves it on. Inferred from the client's documented behaviour, not measured.

identity.account_note: one address can belong to several ChatGPT accounts (personal, team workspace), each a separate login; a known mismatch is drift

companion_note: none — auth.json is self-contained, so there is no splice step and no way for identity and token to desynchronize

policy.rotates_note: a snapshot taken before a refresh is DEAD; the old refresh token was invalidated by the rotation. Profiles must be re-stashed after use, not only on switch-away.

device_auth.setting: Signing in with a code needs device code login turned on in your ChatGPT security settings, or allowed in your workspace's permissions by its admin.

messages.unavailable: device code login is not enabled for this Codex server. Use the browser login or verify the server URL.
messages.expired: device auth timed out after 15 minutes
messages.chatgpt_disabled: ChatGPT login is disabled. Use API key login instead.

device_auth.note: codex login --device-auth prints the link <issuer>/codex/device and the one-time code each on a line of its own, in ANSI colour whether or not stdout is a terminal, then polls for up to 15 minutes. On failure it prints 'Error logging in: <message>' to stderr and exits 1; the messages above are its fixed ones. Like the browser login it revokes the live login first. From github.com/openai/codex at rust-v0.169.0: codex-rs/login/src/device_code_auth.rs and codex-rs/cli/src/login.rs. The setting is from https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth (Login on headless devices). Not run: no runner has an account.

provenance.executed_how: the real-machine workflow on GitHub-hosted runners, with made-up credentials and the vendor's own status command as judge: macOS 15 and 26 arm64, macOS 15 x86_64, Windows Server 2022 and 2025 x64, Windows 11 arm64, Ubuntu 22.04 x64 and 24.04 arm64. No real account was used on any of them
provenance.source: github.com/openai/codex at c0cc9fc (2026-11-12): codex-rs/login/src/auth/storage.rs, codex-rs/utils/home-dir/src/lib.rs, codex-rs/config/defaults.toml, codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs

surfaces_note: all three share one auth.json. Desktop sharing is strong inference, not documented: ChatGPT.app bundles the identical binary and keeps its non-credential state in ~/.codex

lineage.note: the ChatGPT account the tokens were issued for. Unchanged by a refresh, which rotates the refresh token. Shared by every member of a Team workspace, so the provider also requires the same address inside the token.

token.note: emptied in place when the login is cleared, as with Claude
